name: Russia
note: Russia model tree. Politics: the historical path (the power vertical) and five mutually exclusive alternatives (liberal, communist, national-populist, ultranationalist with the LDPR, military), each bringing to power only a real party of the data; alternatives are a counterfactual, not a claim about the parties. Economy, industry, military, foreign policy and society branches build, fix Russia's starting national spirits (data/spirits/rus.json), unlock decisions (data/decisions/rus.json), grant research bonuses and, on alternative paths only, claim land and go to war. Policies named after real reforms are cited; effects are gameplay estimates.

focuses.name: Strengthen the federal centre
focuses.description: Reassert federal authority over the regions and the budget.

focuses.name: The power vertical
focuses.description: Build a chain of command from the Kremlin through the federal districts and the regions. This is the path Russia took.

focuses.name: Federal districts
focuses.description: Group the federal subjects into federal districts, each with a presidential envoy. Created by decree on 13 May 2000.

focuses.name: Party of power
focuses.description: Rally the deputies and regional leaders of the governing party behind the government.

focuses.name: One law for all regions
focuses.description: Bring regional constitutions and laws into line with federal law.

focuses.name: Appointed governors
focuses.description: Regional governors are appointed by regional legislatures on the President's recommendation instead of being elected directly, as from 2005 to 2012.

focuses.name: A dominant party
focuses.description: The governing party holds a large majority in the Duma and in the regional legislatures.

focuses.name: Priority national projects
focuses.description: Spend oil revenue on four national projects: health, education, housing and agriculture, set out in September 2005. Unlocks yearly funding rounds.

focuses.name: Six-year presidential term
focuses.description: Amend the constitution to lengthen the presidential term from four to six years and the Duma's from four to five. The amendment came into force on 31 December 2008.

focuses.name: Governors elected again
focuses.description: Restore direct elections of regional governors, in force from 1 June 2012.

focuses.name: Foreign agents law
focuses.description: Require organisations that receive foreign funding and engage in political activity to register as foreign agents, as a 2012 law did.

focuses.name: Managed pluralism
focuses.description: Several parties sit in the Duma while the governing party keeps control of the agenda.

focuses.name: 2020 constitutional amendments
focuses.description: A package of constitutional amendments approved in a nationwide vote ending on 1 July 2020.

focuses.name: A consensus in the national media
focuses.description: The main national broadcasters present the government's programme.

focuses.name: Liberal opening
focuses.description: Open the political system to real competition. The liberal parties (Yabloko, the Union of Right Forces, later New People) gain ground.

focuses.name: Independent media
focuses.description: Return the national broadcasters to independent owners and end pressure on the press.

focuses.name: Round table with the opposition
focuses.description: Negotiate the rules of a democratic transition with the opposition parties.

focuses.name: Democratic transition
focuses.description: The most popular liberal party forms a government and calls free elections.

focuses.name: Independent courts
focuses.description: Guarantee judicial independence and full civil liberties.

focuses.name: Real federalism
focuses.description: Give the regions back their elected governors and their own budgets.

focuses.name: Open markets
focuses.description: Lower tariffs and invite foreign investment.

focuses.name: A European course
focuses.description: Seek close relations with the European Union and the United States.

focuses.name: An open society
focuses.description: Courts, press and elections that hold the government to account.

focuses.name: Red restoration
focuses.description: Hard times turn voters toward the Communist Party of the Russian Federation and its programme of public ownership and social guarantees.

focuses.name: Workers' committees
focuses.description: Organise committees in the factories and the trade unions behind the party.

focuses.name: Support in the countryside
focuses.description: Win over collective farm workers and pensioners in the regions.

focuses.name: A government of the left
focuses.description: The Communist Party of the Russian Federation takes power and rules as the single governing party.

focuses.name: Nationalise natural resources
focuses.description: Bring natural resources and large industries into public ownership, a stated goal of the Communist Party of the Russian Federation.

focuses.name: Public ownership in agriculture
focuses.description: Bring large farms into public ownership, part of the programme of the party.

focuses.name: Social guarantees
focuses.description: A national health service and guaranteed pensions paid from resource revenue.

focuses.name: State planning
focuses.description: Direct investment through state plans for heavy industry and defence.

focuses.name: Deepen the Union State
focuses.description: Draw closer to Belarus within the Union State and to the other former Soviet republics.

focuses.name: Reunite with Belarus
focuses.description: If Belarus agrees, the two states merge into one.

focuses.name: National revival
focuses.description: Nationalist parties such as Rodina gain from a mood of national grievance.

focuses.name: Patriotic rallies
focuses.description: Mass rallies around national symbols and grievances.

focuses.name: Against the oligarchs
focuses.description: Campaign against the business owners who grew rich in the 1990s.

focuses.name: A nationalist government
focuses.description: The most popular nationalist party forms the government.

focuses.name: Compatriots abroad
focuses.description: Make the Russian-speaking population of the neighbouring states a priority of foreign policy, and claim Crimea.

focuses.name: Control the borders
focuses.description: Restrict immigration from Central Asia and the Caucasus.

focuses.name: An army for a great power
focuses.description: Raise defence spending, lengthen service and raise new divisions.

focuses.name: Break with the West
focuses.description: Turn away from cooperation with the United States and the European Union.

focuses.name: The Crimean question
focuses.description: Press the claim on Crimea: a war goal against Ukraine.

focuses.name: Ultranationalist turn
focuses.description: In a deep crisis, an ultranationalist party gains a mass following and seeks an authoritarian state. This is a counterfactual, not a claim about the party's aims.

focuses.name: A street movement
focuses.description: Uniformed marches and rallies spread the movement in the cities.

focuses.name: Sympathy in the security services
focuses.description: Officers in the army and the security services side with the movement.

focuses.name: Seizure of power
focuses.description: The ultranationalist party takes power, abolishes elections and rules as the only party.

focuses.name: Total control of the press
focuses.description: All media come under state control and opposition parties are banned from the airwaves.

focuses.name: National mobilisation
focuses.description: Universal military training, a war economy and new divisions.

focuses.name: Revanchist doctrine
focuses.description: A doctrine that treats the former Soviet borders as Russia's sphere: claims on Crimea, the Donbas and northern Kazakhstan. The neighbours and the West regard Russia as a threat.

focuses.name: War for the lost lands
focuses.description: Go to war with Ukraine for the claimed regions.

focuses.name: Pressure on Kazakhstan
focuses.description: A war goal against Kazakhstan over its northern regions.

focuses.name: The army steps in
focuses.description: With the state in crisis, the generals prepare to take over.

focuses.name: Military council
focuses.description: The armed forces remove the government. The coup may fail.

focuses.name: Martial order
focuses.description: A state of emergency, a curfew and military courts.

focuses.name: A government of officers
focuses.description: Officers take the ministries; the defence budget comes first.

focuses.name: Return to the barracks
focuses.description: The council hands power to an elected government.

focuses.name: Economic recovery
focuses.description: Rebuild the state's finances after the 1998 crisis.

focuses.name: Restructure the debt
focuses.description: Agree new terms with creditors for the debt left by the 1998 default.

focuses.name: 13 percent flat income tax
focuses.description: Replace the progressive income tax with a single 13 percent rate, introduced in 2001.

focuses.name: Recapitalise the banks
focuses.description: Close insolvent banks and recapitalise the sound ones.

focuses.name: Repay the foreign debt early
focuses.description: Use oil revenue to pay off the debt to foreign creditors ahead of schedule.

focuses.name: A single tax service
focuses.description: One federal tax service and fewer exemptions.

focuses.name: Stabilization fund
focuses.description: Save part of the oil revenue in a fund that balances the budget when prices fall. The real fund was established on 1 January 2004.

focuses.name: Reserve Fund and National Welfare Fund
focuses.description: Split the stabilization fund into a Reserve Fund for the budget and a National Welfare Fund for pensions, as Russia did in February 2008.

focuses.name: Inflation targeting
focuses.description: The central bank targets inflation and lets the ruble float.

focuses.name: Special economic zones
focuses.description: Tax breaks and simpler customs for investors in chosen regions.

focuses.name: A financial centre in Moscow
focuses.description: Make Moscow a regional financial centre.

focuses.name: Pension reform
focuses.description: Raise the retirement age step by step to keep the pension system solvent.

focuses.name: A national payment system
focuses.description: A domestic card network and payment system.

focuses.name: Import substitution
focuses.description: Replace imported goods with domestic production behind trade barriers.

focuses.name: Economic diversification
focuses.description: Reduce the economy's dependence on oil and gas.

focuses.name: Rebuild the industrial base
focuses.description: Bring the factories of the Soviet era back to work.

focuses.name: Energy exports
focuses.description: Expand oil and gas production in Western Siberia.

focuses.name: Modernise Soviet-era industry
focuses.description: Replace worn-out machinery in the old industrial cities.

focuses.name: Roads and railways
focuses.description: A federal programme for roads and railways. Unlocks a yearly regional road programme.

focuses.name: State energy majors
focuses.description: Bring the largest oil and gas producers under state ownership.

focuses.name: Expansion of Rosneft
focuses.description: The state oil company Rosneft acquires Yuganskneftegaz, the main production unit of Yukos, sold at auction in December 2004.

focuses.name: New export pipelines
focuses.description: Pipelines to Europe and to Asia that diversify export routes. Unlocks pipeline projects.

focuses.name: Automotive industry
focuses.description: Joint ventures with foreign car makers in the Volga region.

focuses.name: Steel and metals
focuses.description: Modernise the steel works and smelters of the Urals and Siberia.

focuses.name: Upgrade the Trans-Siberian railway
focuses.description: Double tracks and electrify the line across Siberia.

focuses.name: Aviation industry
focuses.description: Merge the aircraft makers into one corporation and build a new airliner.

focuses.name: Develop the Far East
focuses.description: Ports, plants and roads in Primorye, Khabarovsk and Amur. Unlocks a Far East investment programme.

focuses.name: Nuclear power
focuses.description: Build new reactors at home and for export.

focuses.name: Shipbuilding
focuses.description: Modernise the shipyards of St Petersburg and the Far East.

focuses.name: Sakhalin oil and gas
focuses.description: Offshore oil and gas around Sakhalin with liquefied gas for Asia.

focuses.name: Arctic development
focuses.description: Develop Arctic oil, gas and shipping along the northern sea route.

focuses.name: A national power grid
focuses.description: New power lines and plants for the growing cities.

focuses.name: Modernised industry
focuses.description: The last of the Soviet-era plants are rebuilt or closed.

focuses.name: Agricultural revival
focuses.description: Credit and subsidies for farms; Russia becomes a large grain exporter.

focuses.name: Military reform
focuses.description: Reorganise the armed forces and their command.

focuses.name: Counter-terrorism in Chechnya
focuses.description: Federal forces fight the insurgency in Chechnya. Unlocks counter-terrorism operations.

focuses.name: A pro-federal administration in Chechnya
focuses.description: Hand the running of Chechnya to a local administration loyal to Moscow.

focuses.name: Rebuild Grozny
focuses.description: Federal funds for the reconstruction of Chechnya after the counter-terrorism operation ended in April 2009.

focuses.name: Develop the North Caucasus
focuses.description: Jobs, roads and resorts to end the insurgency's recruitment.

focuses.name: Contract service
focuses.description: Expand contract soldiers alongside conscripts.

focuses.name: Strategic forces
focuses.description: Maintain and modernise strategic forces.

focuses.name: A new air force
focuses.description: New fighters and helicopters, and modern air bases.

focuses.name: The 2008 reform
focuses.description: Cut the officer corps and turn divisions into brigades, as the reform announced in October 2008 did.

focuses.name: Air and missile defence
focuses.description: New air-defence systems around the capital and the bases.

focuses.name: Long-range aviation
focuses.description: Modernise the strategic bombers and their bases.

focuses.name: Rearmament programme
focuses.description: A ten-year programme to replace Soviet-era equipment.

focuses.name: Defence industry
focuses.description: Merge the defence plants into state corporations. Unlocks state defence orders.

focuses.name: Rebuild the navy
focuses.description: New submarines and frigates for the Northern and Pacific fleets.

focuses.name: Airborne and special forces
focuses.description: Expand the airborne troops and special forces as a rapid-reaction force.

focuses.name: New armoured vehicles
focuses.description: A new generation of tanks and infantry fighting vehicles.

focuses.name: Drones and electronic warfare
focuses.description: Reconnaissance drones and electronic warfare units.

focuses.name: Snap readiness exercises
focuses.description: Large unannounced exercises across the military districts. Unlocks exercises as a decision.

focuses.name: A reserve system
focuses.description: A trained reserve that can be mobilised quickly.

focuses.name: Garrison Kaliningrad
focuses.description: Reinforce the exclave on the Baltic.

focuses.name: Arctic brigades
focuses.description: Units and bases for the Arctic coast.

focuses.name: Foreign policy concept
focuses.description: Set the priorities of Russian foreign policy for the new decade.

focuses.name: The Commonwealth of Independent States
focuses.description: Make the CIS the frame for relations with the former Soviet republics.

focuses.name: Partnership with China
focuses.description: Settle the remaining border questions and expand trade with China.

focuses.name: Partnership with Europe
focuses.description: Expand trade and energy ties with the European Union.

focuses.name: Cooperation with the United States
focuses.description: Work with the United States on terrorism and arms control.

focuses.name: Collective Security Treaty Organization
focuses.description: Turn the Collective Security Treaty into a regional organisation with a charter, as its members did in 2002.

focuses.name: Union State with Belarus
focuses.description: Deepen the Union State with Belarus: cheap gas for close ties.

focuses.name: Energy diplomacy
focuses.description: Long-term gas contracts as a tool of foreign policy.

focuses.name: Arms exports
focuses.description: Sell aircraft, air defences and tanks abroad.

focuses.name: Eurasian Economic Union
focuses.description: A single market with Belarus and Kazakhstan, founded by treaty on 29 May 2014.

focuses.name: A voice in the Security Council
focuses.description: Use the permanent seat on the UN Security Council to shape crises.

focuses.name: Visa dialogue with the EU
focuses.description: Negotiate easier travel with the European Union.

focuses.name: A Middle East policy
focuses.description: Ties with Syria, Iran and the Gulf states.

focuses.name: Central Asia
focuses.description: Bases, migrant labour and gas routes in Central Asia.

focuses.name: Turn to Asia
focuses.description: Shift trade and pipelines toward China and the Pacific.

focuses.name: International broadcasting
focuses.description: State-funded broadcasting abroad in many languages.

focuses.name: Alliance with Damascus
focuses.description: Military advisers, a naval base at Tartus and arms for the Syrian government.

focuses.name: Resilience to sanctions
focuses.description: Reserves, domestic payments and new trade partners to withstand Western sanctions.

focuses.name: A multipolar world
focuses.description: Present Russia as one of several centres of a multipolar world order.

focuses.name: Partners in the Global South
focuses.description: Trade and arms deals with India, Africa and Latin America.

focuses.name: Social policy
focuses.description: Set out the government's priorities for health, families and science.

focuses.name: Modernise healthcare
focuses.description: New equipment for hospitals and clinics.

focuses.name: Support for families
focuses.description: Payments for families with a second child, housing help and longer parental leave.

focuses.name: Education reform
focuses.description: A national school-leaving exam and new research universities.

focuses.name: Campaign against alcohol and smoking
focuses.description: Higher excise taxes, sales limits and public campaigns.

focuses.name: Affordable housing
focuses.description: Mortgage subsidies and new housing estates.

focuses.name: Science drive
focuses.description: Grants, research universities and labs that bring researchers home. Unlocks research grants.

focuses.name: A healthier nation
focuses.description: Life expectancy rises and the population decline slows.

focuses.name: Demographic turnaround
focuses.description: Births catch up with deaths at last.

focuses.name: Skolkovo innovation centre
focuses.description: A technology park near Moscow with its own tax and legal regime, announced in November 2009 and set up by law in September 2010.

focuses.name: Space programme
focuses.description: A new launch site in the Far East and new launch vehicles.

focuses.name: Digital economy
focuses.description: Broadband, e-government and data centres across the country.

focuses.name: A sovereign internet
focuses.description: Infrastructure to run the Russian internet separately from the global network.

focuses.name: Bring the researchers home
focuses.description: Grants and laboratories for scientists who return from abroad.

focuses.name: Mining and fertilisers
focuses.description: Expand nickel, potash and fertiliser production.

focuses.name: Black Sea resorts
focuses.description: Roads, airports and hotels on the Black Sea coast.

focuses.name: Timber and pulp
focuses.description: Process timber at home instead of exporting logs.

focuses.name: Black Sea Fleet
focuses.description: New ships and a new base at Novorossiysk.

focuses.name: Information operations troops
focuses.description: A command for cyber defence and information operations.

focuses.name: Aerospace forces
focuses.description: Merge the air force and the space troops into one service.

focuses.name: Dialogue with Japan
focuses.description: Talks on the Kuril Islands and Japanese investment in the Far East.

focuses.name: A gas route through Turkey
focuses.description: A pipeline under the Black Sea to Turkey.

focuses.name: Ties in the Balkans
focuses.description: Close ties with Yugoslavia and later Serbia.

focuses.name: The Arctic shelf
focuses.description: Submit a claim to the Arctic seabed to the UN commission.

focuses.name: Federal universities
focuses.description: Large federal universities in the regions.

focuses.name: Index pensions
focuses.description: Raise pensions with prices every year.

focuses.name: Volunteer and youth movement
focuses.description: State support for volunteer groups and youth organisations.
